coverage.note: GB2312 level-1 (3755 hanzi) plus Latin, digits, and CJK punctuation — about 99.7% of running modern Chinese. A character outside this set renders as a tofu box, not a fallback glyph: for classical text, rare surnames, or names with uncommon characters, verify the render or embed the full face from @fontsource directly.

upstream.note: Authored for VidMuse as hand-written Lottie JSON. Not exported from, traced from, or derived from any third-party Lottie library, LottieFiles asset, or icon animation pack.
Authored for VidMuse. Not derived from any third-party icon or shape set.

offline-logo.hf_usage: Inline SVG or . A mono mark inherits currentColor; a color mark must not be recolored. Keep clear space around it.

icon.hf_usage: Inline the SVG for per-path animation, or reference it with /background-image when it is decoration.

font.hf_usage: Declare @font-face with the frozen local path. Do not rely on the compiler's implicit Google fetch for anything that must render in a distributed/cloud render.

lottie.hf_usage: Load with lottie-web or a dotLottie player, then register the instance on window.__hfLottie so HyperFrames can seek it.
lottie.usage_contract: autoplay: false, loop: false, and window.__hfLottie.push(anim) are all mandatory. Anything left on autoplay/loop runs in wall-clock time and renders non-deterministically. The adapter seeks absolute time — no modulo loop, no playback-rate scaling — so bake repeating cycles into the asset. See hyperframes-animation/adapters/lottie.md.

shape.hf_usage: Inline for morph/draw animation; background-image when static. Tint with currentColor or a CSS custom property rather than editing the file.

sfx.hf_usage: A separate <audio> element that is a DIRECT child of the composition root, with data-start/data-duration/data-track-index.

palette.hf_usage: Feed hex values into a color-typed data-composition-variables entry, a CSS custom property, or a Tailwind v4 @theme block.

LG AI — official mark, color variant.
LM Studio — official mark, mono variant.
Soft melodic chime — gentle positive beat: success/confirmation or a lighthearted transition. Sync to the visual moment.
Crisp UI click — button press, toggle, selection. Short accent, sync exactly to the on-screen action.
Quiet short click — low-key UI tap / soft selection. Short accent, sync exactly to the on-screen action.
Negative / error tone — failure state, a 'wrong' beat, or a glitchy interruption.
Punchy digital glitch — hard-cut accent or sudden reveal. Trigger on the hit; let the decay bleed into the next shot (J-cut).
Harsh, longer glitch — chaotic / jarring transition or a distorted reveal.
Low-key glitch texture — subtle digital shift, minimal transition that sits under other audio.
Bass impact hit — logo/hero snap, headline slam. Trigger on the visual landing; decay carries into the next shot (J-cut).
Bass impact with a short swell — brief anticipation then a deep hit. Place so the peak lands on the reveal.
Single key press — one keystroke / terminal-input beat. Short accent, sync to the typed character.
Notification chime — alert, message-in, toast/badge appears. Sync to the element entering.
Sharp electronic ping — punchy accent on a key reveal or data point. Sync to the beat.
Quick pop — element appear/spawn, chip/tag/badge in. Small precise accent, sync to the pop-in.
Long cinematic riser (~10s build, peak at the end). Trigger at (climax_time − 10.03s) so it crests exactly on the reveal.
Bright sparkle / shimmer — magical reveal or 'shine' highlight on a hero element. Sync to the highlight.
Typing burst (~1.5s of keys) — keyboard / code typing reveal, text-being-typed beat. Start as the text begins typing.
Punchy whoosh/impact — fast reveal or hard transition accent. Sync to the motion.
Cinematic whoosh build (~5.5s) — sweeping scene transition. Align so the swell peaks on the cut.
Short whoosh — quick swipe/slide accent, fast element move, snappy transition. Sync to the motion.
NotoSansSC weight 400 — sans-serif Simplified Chinese, body text.
NotoSansSC weight 700 — sans-serif Simplified Chinese, headings.
NotoSansSC weight 900 — sans-serif Simplified Chinese, display.
NotoSerifSC weight 400 — serif Simplified Chinese, body text.
NotoSerifSC weight 700 — serif Simplified Chinese, headings.
Failure state — red circle springs in, then two strokes draw the cross in sequence. Counterpart to success-check.
Indeterminate loading spinner — a 90° arc making one full rotation over 1s. For work whose duration is unknown.
Determinate progress ring filling 0→100% over 1.5s, starting at 12 o'clock. For work with a known amount.
Pulsing beacon — a solid dot with a halo that breathes out and fades. Marks a live or active point; loops cleanly if you place it repeatedly.
Success confirmation — green circle springs in with an overshoot, then the checkmark draws on. Payoff beat for a completed action.
Sweeping curved arrow for annotation. Stroke-based, so a draw-on animation works.
Right-angle connector arrow for flow and step diagrams.
Proportional fill bar with a track — gives a bare number visual presence.
Irregular organic blob for a soft colored backdrop behind type or a card.
Rounder, calmer blob; reads as a deliberate shape rather than a splash.
Radiating stroke rays. Stagger each ray for a pop-in impact accent.
Solid star burst for a badge, a price tag, or a celebratory accent.
Progress ring with a track. Animate stroke-dashoffset to count a value up.
Four corner brackets — a viewfinder frame that draws attention without a full border.
Ticket-stub container with side notches for a label or callout card.
Dot matrix backdrop. Tiles seamlessly at 20-unit pitch.
Hairline graph grid for a technical or blueprint register. Tiles at 20-unit pitch.
Marker-pen underline for keyword emphasis. Reveal with a left-to-right clip.
Two-pass scribbled underline for a casual, hand-annotated register.
Single-crest wave for a section edge or a scene-to-scene seam.
Two offset wave layers; animate at different speeds for parallax depth.
